scenes.tts: Your blood must grab oxygen in the lungs and let it go in working muscle. How can one protein do both?
scenes.visual: Title fades. A red blood cell drifts from a pink lung toward a red muscle. On screen: How can one protein grab oxygen and let it go?
scenes.narration: Your blood must grab oxygen in the lungs and let it go in working muscle. How can one protein do both?

scenes.tts: In the lungs, the oxygen pressure is about one hundred torr. Oxygen is plentiful there.
scenes.caption: In the lungs, the oxygen pressure (pO₂) is about 100 torr. Oxygen is plentiful there.
scenes.visual: Lung panel with a pressure gauge reading pO₂ ≈ 100 torr. Many O₂ dots around the red cell.
scenes.narration: In the lungs, the oxygen pressure (pO₂) is about 100 torr. Oxygen is plentiful there.

scenes.tts: Blood leaving resting tissue sits near forty torr. Blood leaving hard-working muscle sits near twenty.
scenes.caption: Blood leaving resting tissue sits near 40 torr. Blood leaving hard-working muscle sits near 20.
scenes.visual: Two more gauges: resting tissue ≈ 40 torr, hard-working muscle ≈ 20 torr. Fewer O₂ dots at each.
scenes.narration: Blood leaving resting tissue sits near 40 torr. Blood leaving hard-working muscle sits near 20.

scenes.tts: So blood has two opposite jobs. Load oxygen where it is plentiful. Unload it where it is scarce.
scenes.visual: Two labels on the route: LOAD at the lungs, UNLOAD at the muscle.
scenes.narration: So blood has two opposite jobs. Load oxygen where it is plentiful. Unload it where it is scarce.

scenes.tts: A protein that binds tightly is good at the first job. It is bad at the second.
scenes.visual: A tight-gripping carrier fills at the lungs (check mark) and arrives at the muscle still full (cross).
scenes.narration: A protein that binds tightly is good at the first job. It is bad at the second.

scenes.tts: Predict. Would a protein that binds oxygen more tightly make a better carrier?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: Would a tighter binder be a better carrier?
scenes.narration: Predict. Would a protein that binds oxygen more tightly make a better carrier?

scenes.tts: No. A tight binder fills in the lungs, but it stays nearly full in the muscle. Oxygen that stays aboard is not delivered.
scenes.visual: The tight carrier arrives at the muscle with almost every site still filled. Label: still full = not delivered.
scenes.narration: No. A tight binder fills in the lungs, but it stays nearly full in the muscle. Oxygen that stays aboard is not delivered.

scenes.tts: Myoglobin, the muscle's storage protein, is that kind of tight binder. Across the same gap it would unload only about seven percent.
scenes.visual: Delivered-fraction bar for myoglobin, 100 → 20 torr: about 7%.
scenes.narration: Myoglobin, the muscle's storage protein, is that kind of tight binder. Across the same gap it would unload only about seven percent.

scenes.tts: Hemoglobin gives up about two-thirds of its oxygen between the lungs and hard-working muscle.
scenes.visual: A second bar beside it for hemoglobin, 100 → 20 torr: about 66%.
scenes.narration: Hemoglobin gives up about two-thirds of its oxygen between the lungs and hard-working muscle.

scenes.tts: At resting tissue it gives up much less, about a fifth. Blood leaving resting tissue is still mostly full.
scenes.visual: A third bar: hemoglobin, 100 → 40 torr: about a fifth (about 21%).
scenes.narration: At resting tissue it gives up much less, about a fifth. Blood leaving resting tissue is still mostly full.

scenes.tts: Hard work drains far more. The harder the muscle works, the more oxygen the blood hands over.
scenes.visual: The muscle bar grows as the muscle works harder; the resting bar stays short.
scenes.narration: Hard work drains far more. The harder the muscle works, the more oxygen the blood hands over.

scenes.tts: Both proteins use the same heme and the same iron. So what is hemoglobin doing differently?
scenes.visual: Myoglobin (one chain, one heme) beside hemoglobin (four chains, four hemes). Question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Both proteins use the same heme and the same iron. So what is hemoglobin doing differently?

scenes.tts: Myoglobin has one binding site. Hemoglobin has four that cooperate, and its grip is set for the pressures between lung and muscle.
scenes.visual: The four hemes of hemoglobin light up together; its curve's steep part sits between the lung and muscle gauges.
scenes.narration: Myoglobin has one binding site. Hemoglobin has four that cooperate, and its grip is set for the pressures between lung and muscle.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea for this whole series. Hemoglobin is always a mix of two shapes.
scenes.visual: Hemoglobin icon splits into two silhouettes labelled T and R. A population bar below shows a mix of orange T and teal R.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea for this whole series. Hemoglobin is always a mix of two shapes.

scenes.tts: One shape, called T, holds oxygen weakly. The other, called R, holds it tightly.
scenes.visual: T silhouette with a loose grip on an O₂ dot (label: weak). R silhouette with a firm grip (label: tight).
scenes.narration: One shape, called T, holds oxygen weakly. The other, called R, holds it tightly.

scenes.tts: How full hemoglobin is depends on how full each shape would be, and how much of each is present.
scenes.visual: The population bar with a fullness gauge above each shape; an arrow combines them into one overall fullness.
scenes.narration: How full hemoglobin is depends on how full each shape would be, and how much of each is present.

scenes.tts: Anything that binds one shape better shifts the mix toward that shape. Oxygen itself favors R.
scenes.visual: O₂ dots rain onto the population; the bar slides from mostly T to mostly R.
scenes.narration: Anything that binds one shape better shifts the mix toward that shape. Oxygen itself favors R.

scenes.tts: So oxygen pushes hemoglobin toward the shape that grabs oxygen best. That is cooperativity, and it is why blood delivers.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Two shapes, weak and tight, and oxygen shifts the mix between them.
scenes.narration: So oxygen pushes hemoglobin toward the shape that grabs oxygen best. That is cooperativity, and it is why blood delivers.

scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Two shapes, weak and tight, and oxygen shifts the mix between them.
